story.head: Who’s in net for the Senators?
paras: The Senators (11-6-2) lost 3-2 in overtime to Washington on Tuesday, while the Avalanche have won two in a row. Going in, the Avs are third in the Central (tied for tenth in the NHL) and the Senators fourth in the Atlantic (tied for tenth).

The Avalanche’s record (.632) is about what their chances are worth. The Senators’ record (.632) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.577), largely because they’re 5-2 in one-goal games.

The Avalanche do a lot of their shooting from distance (lowest), play the league’s fastest games (1st) and get their defensemen shooting (2nd). The Senators, by contrast, play slow, tight games (3rd lowest). Colorado has scored 4.11 goals a game, the most in the league. On the other side, the Senators rarely get pinned in their own end (2nd) and get into more chippy games than almost anyone (3rd). Something has to give when the Avalanche’s shooting runs into the Senators’ defense. On top of that, the Senators hit a lot, but the Avalanche mostly don’t.

Nathan MacKinnon (10 G / 20 A / 30 P in 19 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring and is fifth in the NHL, with seven goals in six games against Ottawa since 2023-24. Artturi Lehkonen (13 G / 5 A / 18 P in 19 GP) has a team-high 13 goals, fifth in the NHL. For the Senators, Tim Stützle (9 G / 14 A / 23 P in 19 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Drake Batherson (9 G / 9 A / 18 P in 19 GP) is next in line.

Scott Wedgewood (1-3-1 / .867 SV% in 5 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Colorado, but is expected to start. Linus Ullmark (7-1-0 / .945 SV% in 8 GS) has been outstanding for Ottawa and is expected to start.

items.text: The Senators have been without William Eklund since Oct 8. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Mammoth and the Islanders are missing more right now.

Artturi Lehkonen has 13 goals on chances worth about 7.0 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
